# EDC context index

EDC is a multi-agent coding-assistant toolkit. Use this file to route work to the right deep module docs before reading source.

## How to use
- Read this file first, then use `edc-context/manifest.json` as the authoritative machine routing/policy contract.
- Choose module docs from the table below by changed path or task; for cross-boundary work, also read the coupled modules named here.
- Reports in `edc-context/reports/` are for explicit review/audit workflows, not the ordinary index read path.

## Critical global invariants
- v2 layout is canonical: `edc-context/index.md`, `manifest.json`, `modules/*.md`, `reports/*.md`, `build/build.json`, and the configured root agent entrypoint.
- `manifest.json` is authoritative for routing and policy; human route rows here are guidance, not an alternate router.
- Shell/Node coordinators own build-vs-update decisions, immutable review-candidate resolution, context recovery, review scope normalization, one-probe-per-run source-research capability state (shared into review-all children), task manifests, serial-by-default execution, opt-in concurrency, timeout/cancellation, staged validation, canonical promotion, phase aggregation, structured result/status files, and deterministic validation.
- Models analyze assigned scopes and write declared staged outputs; they must not launch agents, invoke skills as processes, choose subprocess flags, or write canonical context/reports directly.
- Runtime mode comes from `manifest.policy.defaultMode`; rebuild/update flows must preserve operator-authored `policy.*` fields.
- Runtime shell paths remain Bash 3.2-compatible and use normal `bash` resolution; `EDC_BASH` is not part of the public runtime contract.
- Worker artifacts live under `.git/edc/runs/<run-id>/`; canonical context/reports/root review files are promoted only after validation succeeds.
- Pi subprocess workers run with `--no-extensions`; `EDC_PI_EXTENSION_PATH` may add exactly one absolute readable observer entrypoint while preserving disabled extension discovery.
- Octocode is an optional per-run research capability, never an EDC dependency: failed/unavailable semantics are unknown, native tools remain the fallback, assigned evidence scope does not widen, and classifier/manifest routing remains authoritative.
- Nested cancellation deadlines are ordered through one managed policy: worker groups escalate before runtime bootstrap, which escalates before Pi's outer background supervisor; terminal status is written only after termination is verified.
- Workflow boundaries are product contracts: CLI `review`/`review-all` is combined security+delivery+quality over one candidate (serial by default, concurrent only with `EDC_PARALLEL=1`), `security-review`/`edc-review` is security/adversarial, `edc-delivery-review` is goal/spec plus architecture fit, and `quality-review`/`edc-audit` is code quality/maintainability.
- Private implementation prompt bundles must not become public skills; Pi exposes only review/audit/delivery skills while orchestrators can still resolve private bundles.
- Generated context should be high-signal: persist non-obvious contracts, coupling, trust boundaries, and footguns; omit obvious inventories/scratch analysis.
- Published package contents are a supported contract: runtime/Pi/plugin/prompt/docs/license surfaces ship; tests, benchmarks, generated context, and scratch run artifacts do not.
- Runtime code executes only from validated installed-package source or current `HOME/.edc`. Trusted command/Pi wrappers enter through `runtime-bootstrap.mjs`; repo-local `.edc/` is never read, created, repaired, or executed, and Pi installation is global-only.

## Cross-module coupling / blast radius
- `runtime-cli` consumes `canonical-skills` through prompt resolution and embeds review/audit/delivery/build/update wording in subprocess prompts; prompt drift can change worker behavior without changing shell logic.
- `runtime-cli` executes JS helper CLIs owned by `plugin-surface` (`json-cli`, classifier/router helpers, worker manifests/pool, build DAG) and shares worker/bootstrap/Pi timing policy, so inventory/package/global-install drift breaks builds, reviews, or cancellation.
- `plugin-surface` and `runtime-cli` must keep path constants, routing semantics, package/global helper resolution, source preflight, and shell/JS contracts aligned; parity, cache-rejection, install, and package tests are the safety net.
- `agent-wrappers` depends on `plugin-surface` for Pi injection/freshness helpers, runtime-bootstrap access, and termination timing, and on `runtime-cli` for trusted `edc-*.sh` jobs. Its scope/default-base/kill UX affects args and status around review/update/delivery/quality, but not orchestrator routing.
- `canonical-skills` changes affect build/update/security-review/delivery-review/quality-review/audit worker behavior; source workers combine those rules with coordinator capability guidance, while synthesis workers intentionally do not. Benchmark and prompt-contract tests should be considered for wording changes.
- `hardening-tests` are coupled to every module because they encode runtime, package, prompt, route, Bash, ShellCheck, skill-boundary, simplification-ladder, fixture-schema, worker-pool, and Pi behavior as public contracts.
- `benchmarking` is outside normal package/runtime coverage but can drive security prompt edits in `canonical-skills`; keep benchmark-only legacy context paths out of production v2 contracts and pin both worker concurrency and optional research-capability state when comparability requires it.

## Architecture overview
EDC splits deterministic control from semantic analysis. Validated package/global shell and JS code classifies state, routes paths, globally installs managed assets, normalizes review scopes, spawns bounded worker pools, validates staged outputs, promotes canonical artifacts, aggregates phase results, and validates output. Agent prompts perform bounded module/security/delivery/quality analysis in isolated subprocesses.

Trust boundaries: CLI args, hook payloads, Bash command text, Pi JSON streams, git refs, package metadata, config/env values, PIDs/process groups, optional executables on `PATH`, worker manifests, staged outputs, CI logs, benchmark outputs, and LLM-authored manifests/reports are untrusted inputs. Capability probes establish availability only; deterministic validators (`edc-doctor.sh`, `edc-assert-fresh.sh`, `edc-manifest.sh`, worker manifest/pool validation, report validators) remain the canonical gates.
